Hon'ble Vikram D. Chauhan,J.
1.
Second supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.
2. Learned A.G.A. for the State submits that instructions have been received and has no objection in case the bail application is heard on merits.

3. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
4.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that as per the allegations in the First Information Report it is alleged that the plot in question was initially given on lease on 16.1.1993 to one Jantri.

Prior to the aforesaid execution of the lease deed a dispute with regard to Secretary of the society has arisen and as a result of the same Writ Petition No. 21469 of 1992 was filed by the earlier Secretary, Jai Shanker Misra, where the removal of the erstwhile Secretary, Jai Shanker Misra, was stayed by order dated 17.6.1992.

The effect of the aforesaid stay order was that the new Secretary,

sentences.text: It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that subsequently the exchange deed was executed with the Kanpur Development Authority in the year 2010 and the Society itself got the plot in question in the year 2010.
A civil suit was filed by Jai Shanker Misra, erstwhile Secretary of the society, for injunction and the same is pending before the court concerned.
Subsequently, the Society executed the sale deed in favour of third person on 10.1.2023 and on the strength of the aforesaid sale deed, the present First Information Report was lodged.

The submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that the informant is deriving title of the property on the strength of the earlier lease deed dated 16.1.1993 executed in favour of one Jantri who has sold the property to the informant.
It is submitted that even assuming that the lease deed has been executed validly then the title which the informant holds is a lease hold right.
He further submits that the title to the property vests with the society and the lessee does not have the right to claim title to the property beyond the lease hold rights.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the execution of the sale deed in the year 2023 is the transfer of the title of the property and the same infringes the right of the informant who is claiming to be the lessee.

He further submits that the dispute in the present case is with regard to title of the property and it is a civil dispute, therefore, the applicant cannot criminally prosecuted in respect of the same.
The criminal history of the applicant has been explained in paragraph no. 4 of the supplementary affidavit.
Applicant is languishing in jail since 7.6.2023 and in case he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the trial.

5. Learned counsel for the informant submits that the sale deed has been executed in the year 2023 by the society despite the fact that the applicant has purchased the property in the year 2004 from one Jantri to whom the property was transferred in the year 1993.

On a pointed query being made to learned for the informant as to the right under which the aforesaid Jantri holds the property in question, learned counsel for the informant fairly submits that a lease deed was executed in favour of the aforesaid Jantri.
He further submits that in respect of the lease deed, the civil suit is pending for injunction between the society and the informant.
It is further submitted that the informant is in possession of the property in question since the year 2004.
The informant claims to be in possession of the property in question.
6. At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant would not interfere in the possession of the informant.
The dispute is of civil nature.

Although learned counsel for the applicant disputes the possession of the informant and submits that possession of the property has been given to the society on 30.11.2022 by the Kanpur Development Authority, however, he submits that the applicant would not take any coercive measures for seeking possession from the informant except in accordance with law.
7. Learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail but does not dispute factual matrix of the case.
8. Learned AGA for the State has pointed out the criminal antecedents of the applicant.
No material or circumstance has been brought to the notice of this Court with regard to tampering of evidence or intimidating of witness in previous criminal cases.

In Ash Mohammad Vs. Shiv Raj Singh, (2012) 9 SCC 446, the Apex Court in para 30 has observed:-

sentences.text: "We may hasten to add that when we state that the accused is a history-sheeter we may not be understood to have said that a history-sheeter is never entitled to bail.

But, it is a significant factor to be taken note of regard being had to the nature of crime in respect of which he has been booked."
9.

In the case of Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2020 (11) SCC 648, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused may itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari Vs. State of U.P. and another, 2020 (11) SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. In so far as criminal antecedents of the applicant is concerned, it is not the case of the State that applicant might tamper with or otherwise adversely influence the investigation, or that he might intimidate witnesses before or during the trial.
The State has also not placed any material that applicant in past attempted to evade the process of law.

If the accused is otherwise found to be entitled to bail, he cannot be denied bail only on the ground of criminal history, no exceptional circumstances on the basis of criminal antecedents have been shown to deny bail to accused, hence,
the Court does not feel it proper to deny bail to the applicant just on the ground that he had criminal antecedent.
11. The principle that Bail is a rule and Jail is an exception has been well recognised by Apex Court more specifically on the touch stone of Article 21 of the Constitution.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Apex Court in Satyendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51.

entities.text: Satyendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA has not shown any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.

12. No material, facts or circumstances has been shown by learned AGA for the State that the accused may tamper with the evidence or witnesses or the accused is of such character that his mere presence at large would intimidate the witnesses or that accused will use his liberty to subvert justice or tamper with the evidence.
13. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA for the State.
14. Learned AGA for the State has not shown any material or circumstances that the accused/applicant is not entitled to bail in larger interests of the public or State.

15. It is to be seen that in the present case initially the dispute with regard to the Secretary of the society has arisen and as a result of the same an order was passed by this Court staying the removal of the earlier Secretary, Jai Shanker Misra, on 17.6.1992.

However, the newly appointed Secretary,
Mohd. Khan, had executed the lease deed on 16.1.1993 during the currency of the interim order dated 17.6.1992.
Subsequently, the lessee has executed the sale deed in favour of the informant in the year 2004.
Now the society has executed a sale deed in the year 2023 in respect of the plot in question.

The title which the informant claims is not the title that has been transferred by one Ramakant Agnihotri vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87477532/

sentences.text: An individual cannot have a better title than the title claimed by the seller and as such lease could have been transferred in case lease deed is valid.
The society has sold the property in question by transferring the rights of title.
The dispute prima facie is a civil dispute.

16. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, submissions of learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

17. Let the applicant-Ramakant Agnihotri involved in Case Crime No. 0074 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 506, 34 and 448 I.P.C., Police Station Rawatpur, District Kanpur Nagar be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions:-
i.
The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
ii. The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness.

iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted and/or the applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.
iv. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

v. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
vi. The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court.
vii. In the event, the applicant changes residential address, the applicant shall inform the court concerned about new residential address in writing.
18. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.
